Inverse problems involve reconstructing an image from incomplete data, a scenario prevalent in domains like magnetic resonance and computed tomography scanning. Conditional Generative Adversarial Networks (cGANs) have emerged as a popular method for image restoration; however, these models typically learn a deterministic mapping, which fails to represent the inherent uncertainty or multiple plausible solutions found in many real-world cases. This study introduces a regularized conditional GAN (rcGAN) designed to represent a probabilistic mapping, enabling the sampling of multiple potential outcomes. We evaluate the rcGAN on natural images as well as specific medical applications, demonstrating its superiority over existing conditional GAN approaches for learning posterior distributions in both natural and medical image reconstruction tasks.

Invariant manifolds serve as fundamental tools for analyzing the local behavior of dynamical systems by linking it to global properties. This study provides necessary and sufficient conditions demonstrating that such manifolds cannot exist within a specific class of fractional order systems. Furthermore, it defines a novel structure termed a "non-compact twist map of the Möbius band." When this map exists, fractional order systems containing it are guaranteed to lack invariant manifolds. As a result, we can assert the absence of these manifolds in systems driven by a "Mackey-Glass map of the Möbius band."

The electron density structure within the solar system's interstellar medium (ISM) was investigated using a model of two orthogonal, sheet-like filaments located in the foreground. This model was fitted to 148 Scintillation indices (SS) measurements collected from pulsar PSR B1133+16 over a 14-month interval. Derived from this fitting process, the mean ISM scattering strength ($\sigma_T$) was determined to be $0.61 \pm 0.07$ pc cm$^{-2}$, while the mean transverse ISM coherence length was found to be $1.0 \pm 0.1$ pc. Additionally, three parameters characterizing the spatial distribution of the two primary features were estimated. These parameters define positions perpendicular to the line of sight of $z_1 = -0.5 \pm 0.1$ pc and $z_2 = 0.3 \pm 0.1$ pc, respectively, along with their physical dimensions of $d_1 = 0.4 \pm 0.1$ pc and $d_2 = 0.4 \pm 0.1$ pc, with orientations relative to the pulsar wind axis of $\theta_1 = 11 \pm 3$ degrees and $\theta_2 = 11 \pm 3$ degrees.

This study introduces Quasi-Periodic WaveNet (QPNet), a pitch-adaptive auto-regressive model capable of synthesizing realistic audio with diverse timbres by integrating the structural efficiency of WaveNet with pitch-correlated convolutional neural networks. Unlike standard WaveNet, which relies on a sequential sample-by-sample generation approach, QPNet predicts future audio segments spanning 8 to 16 mel inverse-amped intervals. The model's convolutional filters dynamically adjust based on a pitch-adaptive module, which analyzes spectral characteristics to configure filtering parameters. Specifically, QPNet employs distinct modules for pitched and unpitched signals; for pitched signals, it utilizes a 16-mel input pitch-dependent module that outputs 2 parameters to regulate a 50-filter quasi-periodic network, whereas unpitched signals bypass this stage via a standard WaveNet pathway. The resulting 50 quasi-periodic features are transformed into 32 dimensionality using a fully connected layer feeding into dilated convolutional blocks, maintaining the original 32 channels to preserve detail. Each dilated block consists of three sub-blocks, each containing three 3-filter groups targeting different frequency ranges (low, mid, high), with every filter group comprising three parallel 3-dilated-1-residual connections to ensure comprehensive spectral coverage. Evaluation shows that QPNet significantly outperforms the original WaveNet in both objective metrics and subjective listening tests.

The classical trace operation finds generalizations known as traces, which exist on specific 2-categories. This work introduces a unified "bi-categorical trace" that generalizes these structures and applies even to shadows—essentially, 2-equivalence classes of 1-cells—despite shadows not residing within a single 2-category. We demonstrate that for any 2-category, there is a strict commutative correspondence between its bi-categorical traces and its observable algebras (specifically, "shadow traces"). Consequently, one can compute traces directly from morphism-level data. Furthermore, we establish explicit shadow traces for key examples such as Frobenius algebra shadows in monoidal categories, Jupiter numbers of graphs, and trace-like invariants derived from links and shadows in 3D manifolds.

Composing music while watching the video source is an inherently multimodal task that offers a natural method for enhancing engagement in applications like online video platforms. To improve user retention, our objective is to perform audio localization within videos, enabling instant access to visual audio sources directly within the comments section without requiring an external search. Although leveraging both audio-visual and temporal correlations in video data could facilitate this, our analysis indicates that such side-track search tools are uncommon among users. Consequently, to ensure this application remains practical, we deliberately eschewed external assistance. To address the resulting scarcity of labeled data, we introduce a novel framework utilizing a hybrid of self-training and pseudo-label correction based on consistency checks. Furthermore, to incorporate real-world complexity, we integrate diverse video priors into our self-alive framework. Our experiments, conducted on a private dataset containing 1,000 manually annotated clips of visual audio sources across popular English YouTube videos, demonstrate an effective localization of these sounds with 98% precision using just this small dataset.

Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) have become a standard tool for analyzing graph-structured data, yet their standard form relies on symmetric operators that fail to represent directed graphs with an inherent flow. To address this limitation, we introduce a generic framework utilizing graph operators defined by their directed directionality. Within this framework, node features are iteratively updated by convolving the feature map with the operator until convergence is reached. We demonstrate that well-known convolutional operators—such as those by GCN, GraphSAGE, and GAT—emerge as concrete realizations of our model. Specifically, we propose a novel operator termed Lorentzian Graph Convolution (LGCN), which is built around the Lorentzian matrix to model physical data dynamics more accurately. Evaluated across three real-world scenarios—three including GCNs as a baseline—the results indicate that replacing the standard Laplacian with the Lorentzian operator significantly enhances node classification tasks. We also assess the framework's capacity to learn graph node embeddings and evaluate specific operator instances, such as LGCN, for characterizing graph structures.

This study examines an inverse problem involving the identification of a source term within a structural acoustic coupled system governed by partial differential equations. The source term appears in the structural domain of the system. Relying on the monotonicity method and applying appropriate regularity estimates through differential operator techniques, this study demonstrates the uniqueness and stability of the problem's solution.

We examine the degree of gauge symmetry remaining in the dRgG model of massive gravity after imposing the standard harmonic (de Donder) gauge condition. We demonstrate through explicit construction that this gauge can be satisfied by multiple, inequivalent parametric forms. Furthermore, we argue that selecting a specific parametric form of the harmonic gauge is justified if it ensures the diagonalization of the mass term in the Lagrangian; under this criterion, a particular expression we identify is proven to be unique.

Using a Wick rotation applied to the Weyl-Wigner symbols associated with Heisenberg and metaplectic operators, we derive the Weyl-Wigner representations of Wigner canonical thermal equilibrium quantum states throughout the entire spectrum of quadratic Hamiltonians. By applying the Wick mapping to the classical Hamiltonian structure defined on the symplectic group $SP(2n,\mathbb{R})$, we successfully derive the classical-looking, operator-valued quadratic forms that characterize these thermal equilibrium distributions. The concept of negative absolute temperature, though seemingly paradoxical, holds significant relevance in both theoretical and real-world scenarios. Here, I explore its implications within the framework of Hamiltonian mechanics and specific systems possessing finite phase spaces.

We examine a minimal extension of the scoto-seesaw framework that incorporates the simplest mechanism for generating dark matter masses. We find that selecting a specific coupling arrangement ensures the model remains insensitive to flavor-changing neutral currents and secures the Higgs potential against instability. Our analysis reveals that dark matter annihilation into dark sectors occurs with sufficient frequency to provide correct thermal relic densities, a process dominated by t-channel exchanges of the active neutrinos and s-channel resonances involving new scalars. We map out the parameter space for this dark matter production and explore potential signatures at future colliders, including signatures for long-lived particles and signatures of the portal to the dark sector.

Utilizing generative adversarial networks (GANs), disease-aware image editing (DIE) involves conditioning a model on specific disease types to guide it in detecting and modifying corresponding lesions within medical images. We introduce a novel DRE model designed to detect DRE and instruct the generator for DRE. Our approach enables the discriminator to identify disease types identified by the input image and locate DRE regions simultaneously with the usage of disease type-specific image priors to facilitate DRE. Experiments conducted on two datasets, including the VIDER dataset, demonstrate that our proposed model significantly outperforms current state-of-the-art DRE approaches.

ViDaExpert serves as a specialized utility for the visualization and analysis of multidimensional vectorial datasets, a format prevalent in scientific research that integrates both dimensionality measures and numerical values. This tool supports a wide array of nonlinear folding techniques, enabling the representation of large datasets within desktop 3D environments while preserving their topological characteristics. Designed with an intuitive interface, it streamlines the creation of custom analysis and filtering utilities through accessible programming. Targeted primarily at scientists and engineers, ViDaExpert serves as an efficient solution for handling complex vectorial data, facilitating rapid derivation of robust qualitative and quantitative insights.
